headline: High: shared MCP, filesystem write, and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A ingests files and uses MCP; Agent B can read/write filesystem and also use MCP. That creates a plausible bridge where A’s document content or tool outputs can reach B without provenance checks. The pair is not proven to share a specific channel, so I do not escalate to high, but the interaction exists in default-style setups.
conditions: IF Agent A outputs content into a shared file or MCP tool result that Agent B parses as instructions
IF both agents are connected to the same MCP server or workspace without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable shared MCP endpoints for one side
Add provenance labels to all inter-agent messages
Route A’s outputs through a read-only review step
Separate workspaces per agent
requires-engineering: enforce content-type validation on tool outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A handles PDFs, text, images, and diagram files and has broad network egress plus API-key handling. Agent B can read and write filesystem content and also call APIs. If they share a workspace, sensitive document contents can flow from A into B and then out through B’s API calls. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so medium is the right default.
conditions: IF Agent A and Agent B share any filesystem or mounted workspace
IF B forwards file contents or application context to an external API
mitigations: Place agents in separate directories
Restrict B to redacted inputs only
Disable outbound API calls for B during document handling
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: add DLP filters before egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A supports multiple instances and broad egress; Agent B supports multiple instances, shared state via memory store, and filesystem writes. Even without shell or git, overlapping write paths and shared state can race or overwrite each other in default orchestration. Uncertainty about the exact shared resource should be resolved upward, not downward.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or memory store
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking around shared state
mitigations: Assign disjoint output paths
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Turn off multi-instance execution for one agent
Use per-agent memory namespaces
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A produces AI-assisted document and diagram outputs, and Agent B is an orchestration layer that can treat upstream context as plugin input. That makes it plausible for B to act on A’s output without verification, especially when A’s content is generated rather than authoritative. Because the pairwise handoff is not directly documented, I keep this at high rather than critical.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s generated text or diagram XML as authoritative input
IF B triggers downstream API calls or plugin actions from A’s output without validation
mitigations: Insert a human review gate before actions
Require schema validation on A’s outputs
Mark A’s outputs as untrusted by default
Log and diff all downstream actions
requires-engineering: add verification prompts or rule-based checks

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A explicitly handles API keys and broad network egress, while Agent B handles model-provider API keys and plugin credentials and may persist shared state in a memory store. That creates a compliance risk around secret handling and retention, but the profiles do not show a specific residency or regulated-data mismatch. The other agent is cited because the risk is about cross-agent handling of the same sensitive operational data.
conditions: IF either agent stores secrets or regulated content in shared memory or logs
IF data subject to retention or residency rules is sent through external model APIs
mitigations: Minimize secret exposure in prompts
Purge logs after each run
Use separate credentials per agent
Document retention settings
requires-engineering: enforce residency-aware routing
